note: Triennial election of the county council, 1908: polled 27 May 1908 in twelve divisions; the other nine (ten seats) returned unopposed, Killeavy by the sitting member being deemed re-elected for want of a nomination. Returned unopposed. Two seats. W. R. Atkinson, W. Baxter, W. M. Clow, James Grew and W. H. Wright withdrew (Atkinson's nomination paper had also been declared invalid), leaving the sitting members, Johnston and Collen, both described as direct labour candidates, declared elected. Charles Johnston: no party label printed in 1908. At other elections he stood as Unionist (Portadown, 31 May 1911, printed 'Unionist': Belfast News-Letter, 2 June 1911, p. 11 ("Armagh County Council"); candidates in the Newry Reporter, 6 May 1911, p. 5 ("Armagh County Council": withdrawals, contests and unopposed returns)). John Collen: no party label printed in 1908. At other elections he stood as Unionist (Portadown, 28 May 1902, printed 'U': Lurgan Mail, 10 May 1902, p. 5 ("The Elections: Armagh County Council"); labels from the Armagh Guardian, 2 May 1902, p. 2 ("But Few Contests": county council nominations, with labels); Portadown, 31 May 1911, printed 'Unionist': Belfast News-Letter, 2 June 1911, p. 11 ("Armagh County Council"); candidates in the Newry Reporter, 6 May 1911, p. 5 ("Armagh County Council": withdrawals, contests and unopposed returns)).
